plan: In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of what others do. Since I pay the second-highest bid if I win (not my own bid), there's no incentive to shade my bid up or down. Bidding below my value risks losing profitable auctions; bidding above risks winning at a loss. With a private value of $39, the optimal action is to bid exactly $39.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction (winner pays the second-highest bid). In such auctions, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of the number of competitors or their strategies, since your payment doesn't depend on your own bid (only on whether you win and what the second-highest bid is). Bidding higher than value risks overpaying; bidding lower risks losing profitable wins. Therefore, I will bid exactly my value of $34.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy: you win whenever your value exceeds the second-highest bid, and you pay only that second-highest bid, never more than your value. This guarantees non-negative profit whenever you win and avoids overpaying. With a value of $45, I should bid exactly $45 to maximize expected profit, regardless of what Andy and Betty do.
